### Corning Delivers Outstanding Third-Quarter Results(1)


October 27, 2026


CORNING, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[Corning Incorporated](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.corning.com%2Fworldwide%2Fen.html&esheet=54629323&newsitemid=20261026190094&lan=en-US&anchor=Corning+Incorporated&index=1&md5=0c8f376dc3a37122e836971d52e58ef7) (NYSE: GLW) today announced third-quarter 2026 results that exceeded guidance and provided its outlook for fourth-quarter 2026.


**News Summary:**


- **Corning grew third-quarter core sales 19% year over year to $5.08 billion – the strongest growth since the launch of Springboard – and grew core EPS nearly twice as fast to $0.91.**


- Optical Communications continued to drive powerful growth, with Q3 sales up 44% to $2.38 billion; Enterprise Networks grew sales 84%, with Gen AI product sales growing more than 100% year over year.
- Solar grew sales 37% year over year, as production continued to ramp, albeit at a slower pace than anticipated. As productivity continues to improve, so will output and profitability. Additionally, in Q3, U.S. trade action under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 improves the overall pricing environment and demand for U.S.-made solar products. Overall, the company is making solid progress building a more than $3 billion Solar revenue stream.
- Glass Innovations continued to successfully execute its “More Corning” content strategy, driving adoption of Corning innovations and outperforming TV unit, notebook, and smartphone markets, which have been impacted by memory pricing.


- **In the fourth quarter, management expects to grow core sales approximately 19% year over year to a range of $5.2 billion to $5.3 billion and grow core EPS approximately 36% year over year to a range of $0.96 to $1.00.**
- **Corning’s strong third-quarter results and fourth-quarter outlook demonstrate that the acceleration of growth outlined in the company’s**[“20-30-40” Springboard Plan](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.corning.com%2Fworldwide%2Fen%2Fabout-us%2Fnews-events%2Fnews-releases%2F2026%2F05%2Fcorning-upgrades-and-extends-springboard-plan-outlines-new-phase-of-accelerating-growth.html&esheet=54629323&newsitemid=20261026190094&lan=en-US&anchor=%26%238220%3B20-30-40%26%238221%3B+Springboard+Plan&index=2&md5=ac6f24fb11df063936647468c3fab8fe) **has begun.**


- In the third quarter, Corning secured four long-term, multibillion-dollar customer agreements, including with[Verizon](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.corning.com%2Fworldwide%2Fen%2Fabout-us%2Fnews-events%2Fnews-releases%2F2026%2F09%2Fverizon-and-corning-announce-multi-year-multi-billion-dollar-supply-agreement-for-broadband-expansion-and-next-gen-ai-infrastructure.html&esheet=54629323&newsitemid=20261026190094&lan=en-US&anchor=Verizon&index=3&md5=ee4cd21fcbdfa2e4c91e8cbd4bff3d34) and[AT&T](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.corning.com%2Fworldwide%2Fen%2Fabout-us%2Fnews-events%2Fnews-releases%2F2026%2F09%2Fatt-and-corning-team-up-to-engineer-the-connected-world-with-fiber.html&esheet=54629323&newsitemid=20261026190094&lan=en-US&anchor=AT%26amp%3BT&index=4&md5=b949faca79aad1c6befc67b0d5bb00a5) . The company’s growing number of major customer agreements underpins the growth outlined in Springboard.


(1) *Third-quarter GAAP results: GAAP sales were $4.86 billion, GAAP gross margin was 37.3%, GAAP operating margin was 18.8%, GAAP EPS was $0.78, and operating cash flow was $1.06 billion.*


**Wendell P. Weeks, chairman, chief executive officer, and president, said,** “We delivered an outstanding third quarter. Year over year, core sales grew 19% to $5.08 billion, and core EPS grew 36% to $0.91. We expanded core gross margin 150 basis points to 40.5%, core operating margin 310 basis points to 22.7%, and core ROIC 330 basis points to 16.7% – with strong adjusted free cash flow of $661 million, while investing more than half a billion in capital expenditures to address demand for our innovations. Our strong results provide excellent proof points of the acceleration of growth outlined in our ‘20-30-40’ Springboard Plan.”


**Weeks continued,** “We continue to successfully expand our content within customers’ ecosystems and outperform our underlying markets. For example, in Optical Communications, faster adoption of our innovations helped us double our Gen AI sales year over year in the quarter, outpacing GPU unit growth.”


**Ed Schlesinger, executive vice president and chief financial officer, said,** “When we upgraded Springboard in May, we laid out a path to double our annualized sales run rate from $20 billion to $40 billion by the end of 2030. We also expect to grow earnings faster than sales, with significantly higher ROIC and substantially more free cash flow. To support that growth, we have steadily added capacity, backed by long-term customer agreements that share the cost and risk of expansions. As a result, we have been able to grow adjusted free cash flow to $2.27 billion through the first nine months of 2026 while investing to meet demand.”


**Schlesinger continued,** “Looking ahead, we expect our outstanding performance to continue. In the fourth quarter, we expect to grow core sales approximately 19% year over year to a range of $5.2 billion to $5.3 billion and grow core EPS approximately 36% year over year to a range of $0.96 to $1.00.”


**Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights:**


- GAAP sales were $4.86 billion, up 18% year over year. Core sales were $5.08 billion, up 19% year over year.
- GAAP EPS was $0.78, up 56% year over year. Core EPS was $0.91, up 36% year over year. The difference between GAAP and core EPS principally reflects adjustments for hedged exposures, along with discrete tax items. A complete quantitative reconciliation of these and other reconciling items appears in the tables accompanying this release.
- GAAP gross margin was 37.3%. Core gross margin expanded 150 basis points year over year to 40.5%.
- GAAP operating margin was 18.8%. Core operating margin expanded 310 basis points year over year to 22.7%.
- GAAP operating cash flow was $1.06 billion, and adjusted free cash flow was $661 million.


**Fourth-Quarter 2026 Outlook:**


- In the fourth quarter, management expects to grow core sales approximately 19% year over year to a range of $5.2 billion to $5.3 billion and grow core EPS approximately 36% year over year to a range of $0.96 to $1.00.

As a result, the company created a Glass Innovations segment, combining its former Display and Specialty Materials segments. Corning also created a Solar segment, which includes Hemlock Semiconductor Group and the company’s solar wafer and module manufacturing businesses. Optical Communications and Automotive remain unchanged. All other results will be grouped as Life Sciences and Emerging Growth Businesses. **Presentation of Information in this News Release** This news release includes non-GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP financial measures are not in accordance with, or an alternative to, GAAP. Corning’s non-GAAP financial measures exclude the impact of items that are driven by general economic conditions and events that do not reflect the underlying fundamentals and trends in the company’s operations. The company believes presenting non-GAAP financial measures assists in analyzing financial performance without the impact of items that may obscure trends in the company’s underlying performance. Definitions of these non-GAAP financial measures and reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures can be found on the company’s website by going to the Investor Relations page and clicking “Quarterly Results” under the “Financials and Filings” tab. These reconciliations also accompany this news release.


With respect to the outlook for future periods, it is not possible to provide reconciliations for these non-GAAP measures because management does not forecast the movement of foreign currencies against the U.S. dollar, or other items that do not reflect ongoing operations, nor does it forecast items that have not yet occurred or are out of management’s control. As a result, management is unable to provide outlook information on a GAAP basis.

Corning applies its unparalleled expertise in glass science, ceramic science, and optical physics, along with its deep manufacturing and engineering capabilities to develop category-defining products that transform industries and enhance people’s lives. Corning succeeds through sustained investment in RD&E, a unique combination of material and process innovation, and deep, trust-based relationships with customers who are global leaders in their industries. Corning’s capabilities are versatile and synergistic, which allows the company to evolve to meet changing market needs, while also helping its customers capture new opportunities in dynamic industries. Today, Corning’s markets include optical communications, mobile consumer electronics, display, automotive, solar, semiconductors, and life sciences.
